title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy NGC 7469
caption: Interacting galaxies NGC 7469 and IC 5283, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 7469, QSO J2303+0852, Arp 298, Mrk 1514, IC 5283, KPG 575A · constellation Pegasus · about 200 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys catches the barred spiral NGC 7469 in a close encounter with its smaller companion, IC 5283. The pair lies about 200 million light-years from Earth in Pegasus, the Winged Horse.

NGC 7469 is a Seyfert galaxy, one of a class with unusually bright, active centres, and it is classed as a Seyfert 1. It is also a luminous source of infrared light, and a powerful burst of star formation lies buried deep in the zone around its nucleus.

The picture is one of 59 views of colliding and merging galaxies that NASA released on 24 April 2008 to mark the 18th anniversary of Hubble's launch. According to NASA, just one nearby galaxy in a million is seen colliding today. Encounters like this were far more common long ago, when the universe was smaller and galaxies sat closer together.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colours were assigned.
understand.eye: The 33-minute exposure gathers far more light than an eye at a telescope could.

explore: NGC 7469 also appears in catalogues as Arp 298 and Markarian 1514. Most of the anniversary images came from GOALS, the Great Observatories All-sky LIRG Survey, a study of luminous and ultra-luminous infrared galaxies that combines Hubble data with observations from NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope, Chandra X-ray Observatory and Galaxy Evolution Explorer.
alt: A large barred spiral galaxy with a smaller companion galaxy nearby.
